sentences.text: The name Copepteryx combines Greek words for 'oar' and 'wing', describing its oar-like wings that were heavily specialized for underwater propulsion, differing significantly from other pelecaniformes.
Copepteryx hexeris measured about 1.2 meters long, while Copepteryx titan is the largest described plotopterid, reaching an estimated length of around 2 meters.
The holotype femur of Copepteryx titan is 22 cm long and 6 cm wide, twice the size of an emperor penguin's femur.
The genus Copepteryx was first described by Olson and Hasegawa in 1996.
Copepteryx were diving birds that nested on land and had a carnivorous diet.
Copepteryx is classified within the family Plotopteridae and belongs to the subfamily Tonsalinae.
Copepteryx was a flightless bird endemic to Japan during the Oligocene, living from 28.4 to 23 million years ago.
It is debated whether Copepteryx titan is a distinct species or represents the larger males of Copepteryx hexeris.
